explanation: Backtrack over a mutable character array. At each position, try each distinct remaining character once, swap it into that position, recurse, then undo the swap. A per-level chosen set skips duplicate choices.
correctness: Positions before the recursion index form a fixed prefix and the suffix holds exactly its remaining multiset. Swapping each distinct suffix character into the next slot covers every possible next character once; undoing the swap restores the state for siblings. At the end every character has been used, and duplicate branches were excluded.
walkthrough: For ab at position 0, choose a and recurse on the remaining b to emit ab. Undo the swap, choose b from position 1, swap to ba, and emit ba. Restore ab after returning. For aa the chosen set skips the second identical choice at position 0, giving one result. Return a set of strings; the adapter displays a JSON array and compares membership without imposing output order.
edgeCases: repeated characters under the bank extension.
Empty input returns the singleton set {""}; repeated characters yield distinct strings only, not repeated output entries.
timeComplexity: Expected O(n*n!) worst-case time: with distinct characters there are n! output strings, each constructed/hashed in O(n); all smaller recursion levels are dominated by this bound.
spaceComplexity: O(n*n!) worst-case output strings, plus O(n) character buffer/recursion depth and O(n²) worst-case total chosen-set entries retained along the recursion path.
